description: Cell: Smallest recognizable unit
Motif: Characteristic rhythm + interval pattern
Phrase: Complete musical thought, ends with cadence

parameters.function: Complete musical thought, ends with cadence

description: Period: Two complementary phrases
Double period: Extended period structure
Section: Structural unit (exposition, development, etc.)
Arch (rise-fall) (∧): Completion, singing quality
Ascending (/): Aspiration, tension, hope
Descending (\): Resolution, grief, relaxation
Wave (∼): Lyrical, flowing
Static/plateau (—): Contemplation, suspense
Inverted arch (∨): Settling then rising
Climax placement at Within a phrase level: Near the end (~bar 3 of 4)
Climax placement at Within a melody level: ~60-75% through
Climax placement at Within a section level: After development/buildup
Climax placement at Multiple levels level: Local (phrase), regional (period), global (section)
Vocal orientation: Every melody sings naturally, even in instrumental works

parameters.note: Write it as if a voice will perform it — test by humming

description: Immediate memorability: Theme states itself completely in 4 bars

parameters.note: If a listener cannot recall the theme after one hearing, it is not Handelian

description: Broad arching phrases: Long lines (4-8 bars) with clear peak and cadence

parameters.note: The phrase has a shape: rise, crest, descend, land

description: Diatonic emphasis: Mostly stepwise with strategic leaps

parameters.note: The leaps are events, not texture; steps are the connective tissue

description: Triadic motion: Frequent chord-outlining (arpeggiated) figures

parameters.note: The melody implies its own harmony — no ambiguity

description: Syllabic clarity: Designed around text rhythm, even in instrumental works

parameters.note: One note per syllable for declamation; melisma reserved for key words

description: Repeated notes: Declamatory effect for emphasis

parameters.note: Repetition is rhetoric: "Hallelujah, Hallelujah, Hallelujah"

description: Sequence as extension: Sequences lengthen phrases without losing identity

parameters.note: The melody moves forward by repeating its shape at new pitch levels

description: Ornamental da capo: A section return expected to be elaborated

parameters.note: The bones are the same; the flesh is richer

description: Text painting: Melodic shape mirrors word meaning

parameters.note: "Rise" ascends, "fall" descends, "run" melismatizes — the melody IS the text

description: Sequential continuation: A one- or two-bar figure restated a step lower, two or three times

parameters.note: How a phrase travels from its opening to its cadence; the engine of the style

description: Suspension-driven line: The upper voice hangs over the bar and resolves down by step, repeatedly

parameters.note: Dissonance becomes the melody's forward motion rather than an incident in it

description: Paired thirds and sixths: The two violins run in parallel for long stretches, then cross

parameters.note: A single sweetened line that periodically separates into two

description: Conjunct with cadential leaps: Mostly stepwise; leaps concentrated at phrase openings and cadential approaches

parameters.note: Keeps the sequence smooth and marks the joints

description: Modest compass: Rarely above the third position; no extended range display

parameters.note: The interest is the interaction of the parts, not the reach of one

description: Even rhythmic surface: Steady quavers or crotchets, changing value at cadences

parameters.note: The harmonic rhythm carries the drama; the surface stays level

description: Written-out ornament at cadences: Trills and appoggiaturas notated into the cadential formula

parameters.note: The cadence is the ornamental moment, not the phrase interior

description: Arpeggiated themes: Themes built on broken triads and seventh chords

parameters.note: Natural violin resonance; open, ringing quality; immediate harmonic clarity

description: Sequence as structure: 2-bar melodic pattern repeated stepwise (up or down)

parameters.note: Momentum through repetition — the ear catches the pattern and rides it forward

description: Narrow motivic material: A theme may use only 3–4 intervals; repetition generates energy

parameters.note: Economy of means — what sounds simple becomes compelling through rhythmic drive

description: Scale runs: Rapid ascending/descending passages spanning 1–3 octaves

parameters.note: Virtuosic brilliance; physical excitement of the hand moving through positions

description: String crossing patterns: Melodies that alternate between adjacent strings

parameters.note: Bariolage effect; the open string rings against the stopped note, creating shimmer

description: High-register singing: Long, sustained melody in 3rd–7th position

parameters.note: Operatic expressiveness — the violin imitates the soprano

description: Measured tremolo: Rapid repeated notes on a single pitch

parameters.note: Intensity without changing the harmony — the trembling IS the expression

description: Echo repetition: Same phrase repeated piano after forte

parameters.note: Theatrical effect borrowed from opera — the echo as memory or reflection
